summary: Govind Chandra Pande (1923–2011) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He served as Vice Chancellor of the University of Rajasthan (attested 1967) and University of Allahabad (~1984–1987), and chaired the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (~1999–2004).

Govind Sadashiv Ghurye (1893–1983) worked in Indology and other fields. He studied at Elphinstone College and completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge under W. H. R. Rivers (~1920–1922). He held a post at the University of Mumbai (~1924–1959).
Govind Sakharam Kathavate was an Indologist. He held the Sanskrit chair at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, where he succeeded Ramkrishna Gopal Bhandarkar.

Govind Swamirao Gai (1917–1995) was an Indology, history and archaeology, and linguistics scholar. He served the Government of India as Chief Epigraphist (attested 1958–1966) and the Archaeological Survey of India as Chief Epigraphist for India (1966–1976), succeeding Dineschandra Sircar.
Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt was an Indologist. He served as a professor at Baroda College (attested 1933–1939) and later as Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1953–1957).

Grace S. Fong (born 1948) is a sinologist who studied at McGill University and the University of British Columbia (~1978–1984). She taught at Smith College (attested 1986) and McGill University (~1989), where she chaired the Department of East Asian Studies.

Graeme MacQueen (1948–2023) worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his doctorate under Masatoshi Nagatomi at Harvard University (~1971–1979) and served as a lecturer at McMaster University (~1977–2013).
Graham E. Clarke (died 1998) was a scholar of Tibetology. He held posts at the Institute of Development Studies and as a Senior Member at the University of Oxford (attested 1998).
Graham Lock is a scholar in Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied under Hsuan Hua and Saddhaloka Bhikkhu.

Graham Priest (born 1948) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cambridge and the LSE, later holding posts at Melbourne, St Andrews (attested 2011–2018), and CUNY as Distinguished Professor (~2009).

Graves Champney Haughton (1788–1849) studied at East India Company College (~1814–1816), later serving there as Professor of Hindú Literature, and the History of Asia (~1817–1827). He also served as secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1831–1832).

Gray Tuttle is a Tibetologist and historian who earned his PhD from Harvard (2002) under William C. Kirby, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Philip A. Kuhn. He became an Associate Professor at Columbia University (attested 2008–2015).

Graziadio Isaia Ascoli (1829–1907) was a linguist and Indologist. In 1860, he became a professor at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano, and he founded the journal Archivio Glottologico Italiano.

Greg Bailey is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed doctoral studies under J. Durham and was taught by Madeleine Biardeau, later serving as a professor at La Trobe University (attested 1994, 2004).
Gregor Ahn (born 1958) is a religious studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit. He took up a post at Heidelberg University around 2003.

Gregory Forgues is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna (attested 2011) under MA supervisor Helmut Tauscher, and studied under Birgit Kellner and several traditional teachers.

Gregory Max Seton works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Naropa University, UC Santa Barbara, and the University of Oxford (D.Phil 2015), where he was supervised by Vesna A. Wallace and Alexis Sanderson.

Gregory P. A. Levine (born 1963) specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history. Educated at Oberlin College and Princeton University, he became an Associate Professor of Japanese art and Buddhist visual cultures at UC Berkeley (~2000).

Gregory Schopen (born 1947) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He earned his PhD at the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana, holding posts at Brown, Texas, Indiana, Stanford, and UCLA.

Grigorij Maksimovič Bongard-Levin (1933–2008) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies. Educated at Moscow State University, where he later taught (~1978–2008), he also served at the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1956–2008).
